title: The She-Goats and Their Beards
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: Jupiter granted beards to the She-Goats at their own request, much to the disgust of the he-Goats, who considered this to be an unwarrantable invasion of their rights and dignities. So they sent a deputation to him to protest against his action. He, however, advised them not to raise any objections. "What's in a tuft of hair?" said he. "Let them have it if they want it. They can never be a match for you in strength."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who granted the She-Goats their beards?
According to the passage, why did the She-Goats receive beards?
According to the passage, how did the he-Goats regard the She-Goats' new beards?
options: As an unwarrantable invasion of their rights and dignities
As a sign of coming disaster

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the he-Goats do about their objection?
options: Grew beards of their own to compete
Sent a deputation to protest to Jupiter
Challenged the She-Goats to a fight

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "unwarrantable" mean in "an unwarrantable invasion of their rights"?
As the passage uses it, what does "tuft" mean in "What's in a tuft of hair?"?
Based on the passage, why does Jupiter tell the he-Goats they will never be matched in strength?
options: To warn them that the She-Goats are plotting against them
To promise them even longer beards in the future
To remind them that a cosmetic feature like a beard does not change their real advantage
To suggest that strength no longer matters

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Beards are more valuable than strength
Jupiter always sides with the party that complains loudest
It is best to never grant requests from those who ask
A superficial resemblance does not erase a real difference that still matters

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what question does Jupiter ask the he-Goats?
According to the passage, what does Jupiter tell the he-Goats to let the She-Goats have?
According to the passage, what word describes the he-Goats' reaction to the She-Goats getting beards?
As the passage uses it, what does "dignities" mean in "their rights and dignities"?
options: Their sense of honor and status

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why might Jupiter see the he-Goats' complaint as unimportant?
options: He secretly prefers the She-Goats to the he-Goats
He believes a beard is a trivial thing next to their real advantage in strength
He has forgotten that he granted the beards
He thinks the he-Goats should also request beards

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: The he-Goats and She-Goats fight over who gets beards
Jupiter punishes the he-Goats for complaining
The She-Goats give up their beards after the he-Goats protest
Jupiter grants the She-Goats beards, and although the he-Goats protest, he dismisses the matter since their real strength is unaffected
